item.title: France’s Marine Le Pen readies for fight with EU
item.itunes:title: France’s Marine Le Pen readies for fight with EU
item.itunes:subtitle: Far-right candidate promises a ‘trial of strength’ with Brussels in FT interview
item.description:
France’s far-right leader Marine Le Pen is gearing up for a fight with the EU if elected president next year, investors in Accenture cannot decide if AI will be an existential threat or an incredible boost, CoreWeave is chasing insurers’ vast pools of capital, and the US Treasury has fined Bank of America more than $1bn for “egregious and continued” money laundering and sanctions violations. Plus, can Saudi Arabia stop the Houthis?


Mentioned in this podcast:

France’s Marine Le Pen gears up for fight with EU

Will Accenture survive or thrive in the age of AI?

CoreWeave targets ‘unlimited’ insurance money to fund AI build-out

Bank of America fined $1.2bn over money laundering failures

Military briefing: can Saudi Arabia stop the Houthis?


Want to get in touch? Email us at podcasts@ft.com


Note: The FT does not use generative AI to voice its podcasts


The FT News Briefing is produced by Sonja Hutson, Saffeya Ahmed, and Josh Gabert-Doyon. Our editor is Marc Filippino. Our video producer is Zach Alfred. Our show is mixed by Sam Giovinco and Alex Higgins. Additional help from Gavin Kallmann, Michael Lello, Peter Barber and David da Silva. Our executive producer is Topher Forhecz. Flo Phillips is the FT’s global head of audio. The show’s theme music is by Metaphor Music.

item.title: An election supercycle could push Europe to the right
item.itunes:title: An election supercycle could push Europe to the right
item.itunes:subtitle: In the space of 12 months, four of the five biggest EU member states will go to the ballot box
item.description:
The IMF is warning that the world’s leading economies need to take “urgent” action to rebuild their public finances, Pakistan is stuck in a tricky place as its ally Saudi Arabia fights off the Houthis, and Mark Zuckerberg says Meta has caught up with rivals at the “frontier” of AI. Plus, a number of elections in Europe could fundamentally shift the EU, and the UK has imposed new sanctions on Iran over a security incident at a RAF base.


Mentioned in this podcast:

Top economies heading for biggest budget deficits since Covid, IMF warns

Pakistan’s hard choice on Saudi Arabia’s war

Riyadh defiant as Houthis launch new missile strikes on Saudi Arabia

Mark Zuckerberg says Meta has reached AI ‘frontier’

The election supercycle set to drag Europe right

UK imposes new sanctions on Iran over RAF Fairford incident

India’s Narendra Modi faces ‘bitter pill’ as Cockroach protests mount


Want to get in touch? Email us at podcasts@ft.com

item.title: Houthis attack Riyadh airport
item.itunes:title: Houthis attack Riyadh airport
item.itunes:subtitle: Yemeni rebel group kills 12 and injures hundreds in attack on Saudi Arabian capital
item.description:
The Iran-backed Houthis have struck Riyadh airport in Saudi Arabia multiple times this week, US president Donald Trump claims an “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine, and AI companies are pulling back new debt issuance. Plus, US bank earnings this week suggest the good times may be over.


Mentioned in this podcast:

US threatens to block arms for Ukraine over attacks on Russian refineries

Ukraine’s allies vow to pressure Moscow as Trump claims ‘energy ceasefire’ in place

Missile strike on Riyadh airport kills 12 and injures hundreds

Houthis show military reach with deadly missile strikes on Riyadh

AI borrowing slows as investors grow wary of debt binge

Wall Street’s record-breaking trading streak set to cool

item.title: SoftBank wants Gulf money to expand AI bet
item.itunes:title: SoftBank wants Gulf money to expand AI bet
item.itunes:subtitle: Masayoshi Son has held talks with investors in UAE in recent weeks
item.description:
SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son is seeking to raise as much as $100bn from Gulf investors to further his massive bet on AI, the Flydubai co-pilot who tried to hijack a flight to Tel Aviv expressed misogynistic views online, and Donald Trump has said Washington will not strike Iran ahead of the US midterm elections. Plus, two Latvian men allegedly trespassed at a UK military base, and two crypto groups with links to a Trump family-backed company are embroiled in a $141mn legal battle.


Mentioned in this podcast:

SoftBank seeks $100bn from Gulf to expand massive AI bet

The online life of the Flydubai attacker

Donald Trump says US ‘will not be attacking Iran’ before midterm elections

Oil prices jump on tanker attacks and slowing flows through Strait of Hormuz

EasyJet doubles winter flight cuts amid rising costs

Two Latvian nationals arrested on suspicion of trespass at RAF base

Crypto companies linked to Trump-backed firm in $141mn legal battle


Want to get in touch? Email us at podcasts@ft.com

item.title: Oil companies are full speed ahead in the Middle East
item.itunes:title: Oil companies are full speed ahead in the Middle East
item.itunes:subtitle: Western groups look to new investment opportunities despite the chaos and heightened risks caused by the conflict with Iran
item.description:
Oil executives expressed their appetite for investing in the Middle East despite the war, the conflict has blown a near-£12bn hole in Britain’s public finances, and big investors are “bottom fishing” among beaten-down assets, including Italian bonds and corporate debt. Plus, China is building data centres at rapid speed across Inner Mongolia and a measure of credit risk at Elon Musk’s SpaceX rose to a record high.


Mentioned in this podcast:

Oil majors look beyond Middle East war to access region’s vast reserves

Iran war blows near-£12bn hole in Britain’s public finances

Big investors ‘bottom fish’ in Eurozone bond markets after France sell-off

China races to build AI data centres across energy-rich hinterland

SpaceX credit risk jumps on worries over its borrowing spree


Want to get in touch? Email us at podcasts@ft.com

item.title: Skydance’s debt pile takes the spotlight
item.itunes:title: Skydance’s debt pile takes the spotlight
item.itunes:subtitle: Heavy cuts expected as boss David Ellison tries to deliver $6bn of cost savings
item.description:
Paramount Skydance is tackling a huge pile of debt following its takeover of Warner Bros Discovery, oil tanker captains are being paid rates equivalent to $100,000 a month for travelling through the Strait of Hormuz, and the UK’s tax authorities probed Manchester City in 2018. Plus, the battle for control of the $265bn Tata Group hinges on India’s motorbike billionaire, and Brussels is considering taxing big US tech companies through a broad levy on large corporations.


Mentioned in this podcast:

Debt in the spotlight as Paramount closes $111bn deal for Warner Bros

Ships’ captains paid $100,000 a month to transit Strait of Hormuz

HMRC opened probe into Man City’s tax affairs in 2018

India’s motorbike billionaire steering tussle at Tata

Brussels looks to capture Big Tech through tax on large corporations
